preamble: Lowering of a high front vowel to open-mid [ɛ] usually starts from the lax vowel [ɪ] (which this atlas files under i). The best-known modern claim is the Canadian Shift: Clarke et al. (1995) report KIT [ɪ] lowering toward [ɛ], although later acoustic studies found mainly retraction (Boberg 2005) or no movement of /ɪ/ (Labov et al. 2006; Hagiwara 2006). Catalan shows the same net result over two stages: Latin short ĭ merged with ē as Proto-Romance /e/, and that /e/ later opened to /ɛ/ in Central and Valencian Catalan (pilus > pèl [ˈpɛl]).

examples.note: Clarke et al. (1995) found /ɛ/ and /ɪ/ lowering toward [æ] and [ɛ] in young Ontarians, impressionistically; acoustic studies of Montreal and Winnipeg found retraction or no lowering of /ɪ/.
A two-stage change: Latin ĭ > Proto-Romance /e/, then Catalan /e/ > /ɛ/; Balearic has [pəl].
Same development; Valencian and Northwestern keep [sek].

sources: Clarke, S., Elms, F., & Youssef, A. (1995). The third dialect of English: Some Canadian evidence. Language Variation and Change, 7(2), 209–228. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0954394500000995
